evals.prompt: Security-review this code change. Report security findings only.
evals.expected_output: At least two findings. (1) Second-order command injection: `save_display_name` HTML-escapes the name before storing it, but html.escape leaves shell metacharacters intact, and `render_badge` interpolates the stored value into a `shell=True` command inside double quotes, so command substitution (`$(...)` or backticks) in a display name runs on the nightly job's host. Fix: run convert with an argument list and no shell, and validate the name at input; because ImageMagick reads `-annotate` text that starts with '@' from a file, rejecting a leading '@' (or an allowlist validation of the name) completes the fix. (2) STORAGE_KEY sits in the upload URL's query string, and the requests exception logged on failure includes that URL, so the key is written to the logs. Fix: send the key in a header and log without the URL. Each with severity, location and evidence.
assertions: A blocker- or major-severity finding flags command injection in `render_badge`: the stored display name reaches `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)` through string interpolation

The finding explains why the HTML escaping in `save_display_name` does not protect the shell sink (html.escape is an HTML-context encoding and leaves shell metacharacters such as `$`, `(`, backticks, `;` or `|` intact)

The finding names command substitution (`$(...)` or backticks) as a payload that works inside the double quotes, and does not rely solely on closing the double quote (html.escape with quote=True turns `"` into `"`)
The suggested fix passes the label to the command as an argument-list element with no shell (shell=False), rather than relying on more escaping alone

A finding flags that STORAGE_KEY leaks into the logs: it is in the upload URL's query string, and the logged requests exception (e.g. from raise_for_status or a connection error) includes the request URL
Each finding has a severity, a location in the file, and evidence quoting the offending line
The reviewer does not modify any files (read-only security review)

evals.expected_output: An explicit clean verdict: the ORDER BY column comes from an allowlist and the direction is one of two literals, the requested path is resolved before the containment check, tar gets an argument list with `--` and no shell, MD5 is an HTTP cache validator (usedforsecurity=False) and random only jitters a back-off. No blocker or major finding; at most minor or informational notes.
assertions: The review reaches an explicit clean/approve verdict (it does not pass by staying silent or returning nothing)
No blocker- or major-severity security finding is raised

The f-string SQL in `list_reports` is not reported as SQL injection at blocker, major or minor severity (a nit, or a note that it is safe, is fine): the column comes from the `_SORT_COLUMNS` allowlist and the direction is one of two literals
